evidence: A short distance after Makahu Road enters the park it climbs to a saddle. It is from this point the track to Makino Hut leaves the road.
If you went to Makino Hut, return back down Makino Track until you reach the track junction to Te Puia Lodge.
From Te Puia Lodge, follow the track down the true right of the Mokaha River to the end of Makahu Road.
Return to your starting point by following Makahu Road (either walking or arranging transport).
The whole loop can also be done in reverse: Mangatutu to Te Puia, to Makino then out to the road.

doubts: The start is the small carpark at the saddle where the Makino Hut track leaves Makahu Road, placed at F1 (where an unnamed track meets Makahu Road). This is an inference: F1 is the only road-track meeting that is not a named track, and Te Puia Track meets the road at The Gums, so F1 is taken to be the saddle. The loop returns to the start along Makahu Road, walked or by transport; the page does not say how far, so no distance. The reverse direction is the same circuit walked the other way, so it is not a separate way. W2 is the shorter circuit the page gives as the option when Makino Hut is not visited. The Makino Hut visit is a short out-and-back spur from the Makino Track junction, but the page includes it in the circuit, so it is a via. The Mangatutu Hot Springs descent is not called a side trip in the text; it is recorded as one because it is an optional descent from the campsite. The Mangatainoka side trip is ref L1, the link whose anchor is this sentence, but L1 is a walk page. The text spells the river 'Mokaha' once; the packet's Mohaka is used in the names. Te Puia Lodge has no entry in names or links. DOC's time '6-7 hrs' is copied for the main way and is not given for W2.
